run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between 13:49:24 and 14:44:44 UTC on 2026-11-20 the payment-api container in namespace app-100a (Loki stream job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4bwhp) could not obtain database connections: every logged failure reports pool_size 20 with active_connections 20, 7-46 waiting requests and wait_time_ms 5216-26789, together with ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack at PaymentService.processPayment() / DatabasePool.acquire()), and its /healthz endpoint returned HTTP 503 'Health check failed - database unreachable' at 13:57:29, 14:01:50 and 14:44:44. The same container's own 'Database query executed' log lines measured 15-88 ms between 12:30:17 and 13:34:45, 1252-4953 ms between 13:50:55 and 14:43:57, and back to 20-77 ms between 15:01:00 and 15:15:23, so slow database responses are the best-supported mechanism for holding the 20 pool connections. A cluster-wide Loki ERROR count by namespace returned only the app-100a series for 12:00-16:00, and only app-100a/payment-api logged pool-exhaustion or database-unreachable lines in 13:00-15:30, so no other workload is shown as affected. The database itself is not a Kubernetes object in this cluster (no database pod, service, statefulset or configmap was found), so the deepest cause of the query slowdown could not be identified. Prometheus and Jaeger were SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every attempt in this Run and Kubernetes events only go back to 2026-11-21T04:23:43, so no metric, trace or event corroboration exists for the incident and the conclusion is partial. The Nov 21 04:40 rollout of the same deployment is not the cause: the errors are about 14 hours earlier.

claims.text: Log lines from the payment-api container in namespace app-100a report repeated connection-pool exhaustion from 2026-11-20T13:49:24Z to 2026-11-20T14:43:57Z: message 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests between 7 and 46 and wait_time_ms between 5216 and 26789.

The same pod logged 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' with error_code DB_CONN_001 and stack_trace 'at PaymentService.processPayment() / at DatabasePool.acquire()' at 2026-11-20T13:50:55Z, 14:04:41Z, 14:08:14Z, 14:18:41Z and 14:43:57Z.

The pod's health endpoint failed with 'Health check failed - database unreachable', endpoint /healthz, status_code 503 and response_time_ms 5009, 9684 and 6354 at 2026-11-20T13:57:29Z, 14:01:50Z and 14:44:44Z respectively.

The container's own 'Database query executed' log lines measured duration_ms 30, 61, 18, 88, 15 and 65 between 12:30:17Z and 13:34:45Z; 1252 at 13:50:55Z, 3106 at 14:28:27Z, 4953 at 14:30:57Z, 4472 at 14:37:32Z and 2355 at 14:43:57Z; and 40, 20, 54, 77 and 41 between 15:01:00Z and 15:15:23Z on 2026-11-20.

The app-100a error burst is bounded: an ERROR-filtered query over 13:30-13:50 returned only the 13:49:24Z line, the Loki ERROR count_over_time series has no sample before its 13:49:52Z point and runs to 14:49:36Z, and an ERROR-filtered query over 14:44-23:59 returned only the 14:44:44Z health-check line.

Before the error burst the pod logged normal DEBUG 'Cache operation' lines at 13:37:17Z, 13:40:51Z and 13:43:12Z and INFO 'Payment processed successfully' (processing_time_ms 468) plus 'User authenticated' at 13:31:51Z; during the incident it still logged successful payments at 14:07:40Z (processing_time_ms 389) and 14:09:43Z (processing_time_ms 323).

Only one namespace showed errors: a cluster-wide Loki sum by (namespace) of count_over_time(... |= "ERROR" [10m]) over 12:00-16:00 returned a single series labelled namespace app-100a, and a cluster-wide query for pool-exhaustion/database-unreachable text over 13:00-15:30 returned 16 lines, all from job=payment-api service=payment-api in app-100a.

No database workload exists in this cluster as read: the pod list contains 34 pods across namespaces with no database pod, the only StatefulSet is alertmanager in otel-demo, of 30 services the only payment-named one is otel-demo/payment on port 8080 (a different application from app-100a payment-api), the 22 ConfigMaps include none for payment or a database, and namespace app-100a has only Service loki (no Service for payment-api).

The payment-api-100a Deployment in app-100a has generation 1 and creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T04:40:23Z, runs image python:3.9-slim with command python /app/app-direct-push.py, exposes livenessProbe httpGet /healthz on port 8080 with failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10 and timeoutSeconds 10, has a 256Mi memory limit, and mounts /app from a secret (secret contents not readable).

The running pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4bwhp is phase Running with restartCount 0, startTime 2026-11-21T04:40:24Z, owned by ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445, which the Deployment scaled from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T04:40:23Z; the Deployment reports 1/1 ready replicas.

Kubernetes event retention available to this investigation begins at 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z: the returned event set starts there, the app-100a events are only the 04:40Z Nov 21 rollout (Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started), and no event exists for 2026-11-20 13:45Z.

The total number of app-100a log lines per 5-minute step stayed low through the onset of the incident, 1-4 lines between 12:05 and about 14:00, and rose to 3-8 lines between about 14:00 and 15:00, a change consistent with the added error lines.

The otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap lists payment-related fault flags paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable') but every flag in demo.flagd.json, including those two, has defaultVariant 'off' as read; these flags belong to the otel-demo services, not to the app-100a payment-api.

The most likely mechanism is database-side slowness: query durations measured by the app rose from 15-88 ms (12:30-13:34) to 1.2-5.0 s exactly during the 13:49-14:44 failure window and returned to 20-77 ms by 15:01, and multi-second queries would hold the 20 pool connections long enough to produce active_connections 20/20 with 7-46 waiting requests, ConnectionPoolExhausted and /healthz 503 'database unreachable'. The slow database is the dependency to pursue, but it is not identifiable from the evidence.

An alternative or additional cause is that the application failed to release connections (leak or missing close in PaymentService.processPayment()), since every sampled failure shows active_connections fixed at the full pool_size 20 while waiting_requests varies 7-46; the supplied log lines cannot separate 'every connection busy with a slow query' from 'every connection leaked', and no pool metrics were obtainable.

Because the container answers livenessProbe on /healthz:8080 with failureThreshold 3, periodSeconds 10 and timeoutSeconds 10, the 503 responses with 5.0-9.7 s response times could have caused kubelet to restart the container during the incident; whether a restart happened is unverified because no events or logs from the incident-era pod instance survive.

Not all payment traffic failed during the window: the same container logged 'Payment processed successfully' with payment_id PAY-5221 at 14:07:40Z (processing_time_ms 389) and PAY-3838 at 14:09:43Z (processing_time_ms 323), so the degradation was intermittent rather than a total outage in the log sample.

The 2026-11-21T04:40Z rollout of Deployment payment-api-100a (ReplicaSet payment-api-100a-64dcc58445 scaled 0 to 1, new pod started 04:40:24Z with restartCount 0) is not the cause of the 2026-11-20 incident: it occurred about 14 hours after the 13:49-14:44Z error burst, and the error lines carry the same pod_name label on 2026-11-20.

A cluster-wide fault affecting other workloads is not supported: the cluster-wide Loki ERROR count by namespace returned only the app-100a series for 12:00-16:00, and the only pool-exhaustion/database-unreachable lines in 13:00-15:30 came from app-100a/payment-api.

Identify and instrument the database that app-100a/payment-api depends on (the app script is mounted from a Secret and nothing in the cluster shows a database): capture its query latency, connection count and limits for 13:45-14:50 on 2026-11-20 to confirm the slow-query hypothesis, and check the pool configuration and connection-release paths in PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire() (pool_size 20) to rule out a leak.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every attempt in this Run (get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no ERROR rate, latency baseline or Kubernetes state metric could be read; the metric and label names that could show this and were not observable are traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,span_name,status_code}, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{service_name,rpc_service,rpc_method,rpc_grpc_status_code}, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, app_payment_transactions_total and kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{namespace,deployment}.

Jaeger was unavailable for every attempt (traces_list_services and traces_search both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level error status, parent-child call edge or dependency latency could be checked for the payment-api or the otel-demo payment service.

Kubernetes events for 2026-11-20 13:45Z do not exist in this cluster: event retention as returned begins at 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z, so whether the pod's liveness probe restarted the container, or what its pod status and readiness were during the incident, is unknown.

A pod-log read for payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4bwhp over 13:00-14:30 returned no data (status no_data, with the note that no previous container instance exists), so that pod's own node-side logs could not be used; all log evidence comes from the Loki store instead. A Loki query for warn|leak|saturat|throttl|restart|deploy|started|shutdown|signal over app-100a for 08:00-18:00 on 2026-11-20 returned no lines (status no_data), so no startup, shutdown or leak message is available to confirm or exclude a container restart or a leak. A cluster-wide ConfigMap query filtered to names matching payment|db|postgres|mysql|redis|valkey returned no data (status no_data) over 22 ConfigMaps processed.

The database dependency is not identified: log lines say only 'database', no hostname, service or endpoint appears, and no database pod, service, statefulset or ConfigMap exists in the cluster, so what made queries slow (database side, network, or a stalled DB host) cannot be determined. The application script is mounted from a Kubernetes Secret that cannot be read, so the pool settings and query code could not be verified.
change_history is not integrated, so no deployment, configuration or database change around 2026-11-20 13:45Z can be confirmed or excluded.

The incident-era pod instance cannot be inspected: Loki lines for 2026-11-20 carry pod_name payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-4bwhp, but the live pod with that name started 2026-11-21T04:40:24Z after a rollout of a Deployment created 2026-11-21T04:40:23Z, so that pod's previous-container state and restart count describe the later instance, not the Nov 20 one.
next_steps: Check the external database's own monitoring for the 2026-11-20 13:45-14:50 UTC window (query latency, max connections, locking) to confirm or refute the slow-query hypothesis.

Review the payment-api application source and connection-pool settings (the /app script comes from a Secret) for pool_size 20, acquire timeouts and connection release in PaymentService.processPayment()/DatabasePool.acquire().
Correlate with change history (not integrated here) for any database-side or payment-api-side change shortly before 13:49 UTC.
Re-run Prometheus and Jaeger queries when those sources are reachable to obtain trace error status and latency for payment-api and to establish a metric baseline.
